solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tattered Flodden flag, foot missing, as museum piece

definitions.note: adverbial phrase standing for the adjective

indicators.note: something tattered is torn and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
a foot is abbreviated in measurements, and missing tells us that abbreviation is dropped from the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: A tattered banner from the Battle of Flodden, its bottom torn away, displayed in a museum.
explanation.walkthrough: Flodden flag loses one F before being rearranged. Flodden was a 1513 battle between England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-fangled is an old word for old-fashioned, which is what an exhibit kept in a museum typically is.

clue.text: Rare piny variety of chenar below lake

indicators.note: a variety is a different form of the same thing, so these letters take another order
in a down clue, below puts the first piece underneath the one that follows it

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake
a chenar is an oriental plane tree; its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusual pine-like kind of plane tree is growing beneath a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'below lake' puts the lake's letter on top. 'Rare' belongs to the definition: the dictionary marks the word as rare.
explanation.definitionFit: Larchen is a rare adjective meaning of or like larch, a conifer, so it is a seldom-used word for piny.

clue.text: Acrylic fabric in drawer cut lengthwise (not good)

parts.note: drawer cut short to Dr, its banking abbreviation

indicators.note: not good asks us to take away the letter that stands for good

parts.note: along means lengthwise, in the direction of the length
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Some acrylic cloth in a drawer has been cut along its length, spoiling it.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr is the abbreviation for the drawer of a cheque. The surface's chest of drawers is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Dralon is a trade name for an acrylic fibre used in upholstery fabric.

clue.text: Female bird? Not necessarily

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: Is that a hen? Not necessarily, since the bird might be male.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds a female plus a bird; the whole clue then defines it, with 'Not necessarily' warning that it need not be a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: A fowl is a domestic bird such as a chicken, which may be a hen or a cock.

clue.text: Is rationing so far limiting rising tax?

indicators.note: to limit is to hem in, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: as in 'as far', meaning so far

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a toll is a charge or tax

explanation.surface: A question whether rationing up to now has been keeping a growing tax in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is rationing' must be read as one verb phrase, 'rations out', not as the start of a question.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out in portions, which is what someone rationing does.

clue.text: Low-income groups e.g. spend freely with Europe? (9, three words)

indicators.note: doing something freely means without restriction, so these letters are let loose into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
EU, the European Union

explanation.surface: Do the poor spend money freely, maybe with European help?
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is French, borrowed into English dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Gens de peu is French for people of little means, humble folk, so a low-income group.

clue.text: It'll excite change in general and cause end of inaction

parts.note: to leave in the sense of to cause to be, as in 'it leaves me tired'

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of inaction

explanation.surface: Something will stir change across the board and finish off idleness.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the long front phrase; 'cause' takes the sense of leave meaning to make something be so.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaven is yeast that makes dough rise, and figuratively anything that transforms the whole mass it works through.

clue.text: I do act criminally

indicators.note: acting criminally means acting wrongly, so the letters go astray into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A confession of a life of crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: the bandit himself speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacoit is an armed robber in India or Burma, someone who acts criminally by trade.

clue.text: Dull lecturer accepted by group

indicators.note: a thing accepted by a body is taken inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a band is a group
L is the abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: A tedious academic is taken on by a society or a pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland means lacking flavour or interest, a synonym of dull.

clue.text: Odd bits of statue missing in counterfeit? That's absent- mindedness

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a forgery is a counterfeit

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are singled out here, to be thrown away by the word that follows
missing means those odd-placed letters are gone, so only the even ones are kept

parts.note: statue without its first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A counterfeit statue with pieces missing, and someone forgot something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd bits ... missing' removes the odd-placed letters, keeping the even ones. The word is a jocular coinage on the pattern of memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Forgettery is a humorous word for a poor memory, a capacity for forgetting, hence absent-mindedness.

clue.text: Time out from sentry-go, describing evidence verbally

indicators.note: out from means taken away from, so a letter is removed

parts.note: sentry-go is a sentry's duty of walking a beat, a patrol
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A break in guard duty, during which someone speaks of the evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: Sentry-go is an old term for a sentry's duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Parol is a legal term for spoken rather than written, as in parol evidence given by word of mouth.

clue.text: Buzzer, one interrupting doss-house (not quiet), making you cross

parts.note: a bee buzzes

indicators.note: something interrupting breaks into the middle, so it goes inside
not quiet asks for the letter meaning quiet in music to be taken away

parts.note: a flop or flophouse is a cheap lodging house
p, piano, is quiet in music
a means one

explanation.surface: A buzzing noise and someone barging into a quiet hostel would make anyone angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an angry adjective, but it is a noun: a hybrid animal. A doss-house is a cheap lodging house.
explanation.definitionFit: A beefalo is a hybrid bred from buffalo (bison) and domestic cattle, so it is a cross.

clue.text: Fluellen's dust-up: Welsh parlance shows this clan he's upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are taken away

explanation.surface: Fluellen's quarrel: his Welsh way of speaking shows this clan he is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: the answer ('this') plus clan he's, jumbled, make Welsh parlance. Fluellen is the Welsh captain in Shakespeare's Henry V, who pronounces brawl with a P.
explanation.definitionFit: Prawle is Fluellen's Welsh-accented form of brawl, a noisy quarrel or dust-up.

clue.text: Flowering climber flaps so, air becoming agitated

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A climbing plant flaps about in the turbulent wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Passiflora is the genus of passion flowers, climbing plants with showy blooms.

clue.text: Name former racing driver I missed in modern version of his sport

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name

indicators.note: something missed is left out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: Alberto Ascari, Italian world motor-racing champion of the 1950s
taken as written

explanation.surface: Name an old racing driver I left out of a modern form of motor sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the driver in the wordplay: 'his sport' is motor racing.
explanation.definitionFit: NASCAR is the American stock-car racing association and the racing it runs, a present-day branch of motor sport.

clue.text: Like art given licence in French article — quite revealing!

parts.note: deco, describing the art deco style

indicators.note: in places the permission inside the French word

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
let means allow, so licence or permission

explanation.surface: An artwork given permission to appear in a French newspaper article is very risqué.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like art' stands for the style adjective from art deco. The permission sits inside the French article after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Décolleté describes a low-cut neckline, one that reveals a good deal of neck and shoulders.

clue.text: Secret society garment, coating number

indicators.note: a coating covers all round, so the garment wraps the other piece

parts.note: tog, a garment, usually in togs
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A secret society's uniform covers its membership number.
explanation.definitionFit: A tong is a Chinese secret society or brotherhood, often associated with organised crime.

clue.text: Young pig is briefly getting warmed up, tail removed

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, and removed means it is cut away

parts.note: is shortened to 's
hotted up means warmed up

explanation.surface: A piglet is being warmed up, with its tail docked.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail sounds like the pig's; it is the last letter of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotte, also shot or shote, is a young weaned pig.

clue.text: In retirement, nourished with fish? That's got to be believed (6, two words)

definitions.note: a phrase standing for an adjective

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, going back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: fed means nourished
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A retired person well fed on fish: hard to credit.
explanation.walkthrough: The ide, or orfe, is a fish of the carp family, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: De fide is Latin for 'of the faith', describing a doctrine that Catholics are required to believe.

clue.text: Ecstatic about unfolding scene getting on

indicators.note: unfolding opens something out and changes its shape, so these letters are rearranged
about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: sent means carried away, ecstatic
the letters of scene rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by a scene unfolding before them as it progresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting on' looks like progressing; it means growing old.
explanation.definitionFit: Senescent means growing old, and getting on is an idiom for ageing.

clue.text: English ensign at sea, more than one with tender behind?

definitions.text: more than one with tender behind?

indicators.note: at sea means confused and lost, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
the letters of ensign rearranged

explanation.surface: An English flag at sea, flown by several ships with small boats trailing behind.
explanation.walkthrough: A tender sounds like a boat following a ship, but it is the coal truck behind a steam locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam locomotives, called engines, pulled a tender carrying fuel and water; the question mark flags the plural and the example.

clue.text: Relief following Queen's feelings of sickliness

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the first-named piece goes second

parts.note: Qu is an abbreviation for queen
alms are charitable relief for the poor

explanation.surface: A monarch feels sick and is relieved afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Qualms are, in their older sense, sudden bouts of faintness or nausea, not only pangs of conscience.

clue.text: In jug, wretchedly poor, new inside — advocate required

indicators.note: inside places the new letter within the jumbled word
wretchedly means in a sorry state, so these letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: pent means shut in, as one is in jug, slang for prison
the letters of poor rearranged
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A destitute newcomer in prison needs a lawyer to speak for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In jug' gives a single word meaning imprisoned, which then holds the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A proponent is one who puts forward or supports a cause, an advocate.

clue.text: One seen on cavalry horse — could be a hack, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear points to what is spoken, so the word only has to sound right

parts.note: a hack is a jobbing writer

explanation.surface: A rider on a cavalry horse might be riding a hack.
explanation.walkthrough: A hack is also a horse for riding, which fits the cavalry picture, but here it is a hack writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reiter was a German mounted soldier of the 16th and 17th centuries, a cavalryman.

clue.text: Like part of trousseau, look, one that's worn on top? (6, two words)

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top sends that piece to the head of the column

parts.note: clothes worn are on
lo means look!
an means one

explanation.surface: A bride's outfit: look at one that is worn over the top, perhaps a veil.
explanation.walkthrough: The bride's tradition is something old, something new, something borrowed, something blue.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's trousseau traditionally includes something borrowed, an item lent to her for the day.

clue.text: A label stuck in middle of cheese: 'It's right to tuck in'

indicators.note: stuck in means pushed inside something else
the middle of a word is its central letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the central pair of letters of cheese
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A label stuck into a cheese announces that you are allowed to eat it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuck in' here means graze, said of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Eatage is the right to graze cattle on a piece of land, a grazing right.

clue.text: Grand chap (not low) appearing in drag? The opposite

indicators.note: the reverse of appearing in means the second word goes inside the first
not low asks for that word's letters to be taken away

parts.note: a fellow is a chap
taken as written
to lug is to drag

explanation.surface: A dignified man, not at all lowly, turning up dressed as a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' looks like an adjective but means a grand piano. 'The opposite' turns 'chap in drag' around.
explanation.definitionFit: Flügel is the German word for a grand piano, named for its wing shape.

clue.text: Easier high-jump challenge (women excluded) affecting anatomical part?

indicators.note: excluded means shut out, so the letter for women is dropped

parts.note: a low bar is an easier jump to clear
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Lowering the bar for an easier jump, with women barred, might cause an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as one example of the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobar means relating to a lobe, as of the lung in lobar pneumonia, so it affects a part of the body.

clue.text: Committed, even when having to keep silence

indicators.note: having means holding, so the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: ene is an old form of even, the evening
to gag is to keep someone silent

explanation.surface: Pledged to something, even if that means staying quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Even is the noun meaning evening, as in eventide, not the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Engagé is borrowed from French for committed, especially politically or morally involved.

clue.text: Cob nut?

explanation.walkthrough: Read together, a cobnut is a hazelnut; apart, they are two meanings. Loaf for head comes from rhyming slang, loaf of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A cob is a small round bread loaf, and both nut and loaf are slang for the head.

clue.text: Cereal disease, part of fungus mutating

indicators.note: part of tells us the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the word break

explanation.surface: A disease of grain crops is caused by a fungus that keeps changing.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is a fungal disease of cereals such as wheat that turns the grains to black powder.

clue.text: Religious devotee, twice deceased

indicators.note: twice means the same word must be used two times over with different meanings

parts.note: ob., obiit, Latin for 'died', seen on gravestones
the late means the deceased

explanation.surface: A devout believer who died two times over.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblate is a layperson dedicated to religious life, often attached to a monastery.

clue.text: Caravan-owner? Lots going on right-hand side

parts.note: ro, recto, the right-hand page of a book
many means lots

explanation.surface: A caravan site with many vans parked on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: Ro is short for recto, the right-hand page of an open book.
explanation.definitionFit: Romany people are traditionally travellers living in horse-drawn caravans; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Jack in steamrollers (only half working) for aero engines

indicators.note: in places the card inside the rearranged letters
working means in operation and moving, so these letters are rearranged
only half means the rest of that long word is discarded

parts.note: taken as written
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

explanation.surface: A worker called Jack in a road crew where only half the steamrollers run.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of steamrollers, six letters, is rearranged and the J goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramjet is a jet engine that compresses air by forward motion alone, used to power aircraft and missiles.

clue.text: Earth burrows in a core of turf? This bores holes

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something burrowing in digs its way inside
the core of a word is its central letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the central letters of turf
Ge is the Greek earth goddess, so earth

explanation.surface: Soil burrowing into a lump of turf, from a tool that makes holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bores' hints at tedium, but it is drilling.
explanation.definitionFit: An auger is a tool with a spiral bit for drilling holes in wood or the ground.

clue.text: Possible start of film career — secret's blown about part in Hospital?

indicators.note: a blown secret is scattered and out of control, so the letters are rearranged
about means around, so the jumbled word goes round the department

parts.note: the letters of secret's rearranged
ENT, the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: An aspiring actor's secret is out: they had a part in a hospital drama.
explanation.walkthrough: A part in a hospital is a department, not a role.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen test is a filmed audition, which can launch a movie career.
